text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Sunday in Vilnius that Europe would not be safe until the Baltics were safe and and that the three countries remained serious candidates for NATO membership.
- Two Lithuanian basketball teams played for 24 bours, 21 minutes and ten seconds. The event's organisers believe that a world record has been set. The final score was 3,276 to 3,192.
- Ninety-eight illegal migrants and refugees escaped from the Pabrade refugee centre at the week-end. As of Sunday night, 45 had been caught.
- Tourist revenues in Lithuania in 1996 reached 1.3 billion litas and accounted for five percent of the country's GDP.
- A recent poll conducted by the social research centre showed that the country's state-run banks are considered to be more reliable than those in the private sector.

- Confectionary maker Kraft Jacob Suchard Lithuania said that its production figures for the first six months of the year rose by eight percent compared to the same period last year but did provide exact figures.

- The European Commission has recommended that Estonia begin talks for EU membership though its own forecasts clearly show that Lithuania's economy has the highest potential for growth among the three Baltic countries.
- The European affairs ministry introduced its investment promotion programme. The ministry hopes to attract no less than $1 billion in foreign direct investment between now and the year 2000.
- The Medicine Bank reported a 346,000 litas net profit for the first half of 1997.
- The State Commercial Bank posted a 6.1 million litas profit in the first half of 1997. The bank had a staggering 172.8 million litas loss last year.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas and parliamentary chairman Vytautas Landsbergis begin their three week vacations today. They will both spend their vacations on the Lithuanian coast.
- Forty companies have bid for the tender to be lead advisor to the government on the privatisation of the Lithuanian Sea Shipping company and the Klaipeda Stevedoring company.
